Here is the high-efficiency, low-cost production plan for your "Ames HQ" wall:

1. The Material: The "Pro" Budget Choice

Instead of cardboard (which will sag over time with your 3D-printed hooks), go to a hardware store in Ames (Home Depot or Menards) and buy 1/8-inch Hardboard (Masonite).

  • A $4' \times 8'$ sheet costs roughly $15–$20 and can make eight IKEA-sized boards.
  • This brings your cost down from $30 per board to roughly $2.50 per board.

2. The Production Line: The 3D-Printed Drill Guide

Since you have the Bambu Lab A1, you are going to print a "Master Drill Jig."

  • The Jig Design: Print a plate that covers a $200\text{ mm} \times 200\text{ correspondence}$ area. Incorporate "locating pins" that fit into the holes you just drilled to perfectly align the next set.
  • The Math: SKÅDIS uses a $40\text{ mm}$ grid pitch.
  • The "Stacking" Technique: Clamp three or four sheets of hardboard (or heavy cardboard) together. Use your jig on the top sheet. By drilling through the stack, you produce four boards for the labor of one.

3. The Tool: The "Clean Hole" Secret

Standard drill bits will tear cardboard or hardboard. For mass production, use one of these:

  • For Cardboard: Use a Hollow Punch Set. You hit it with a mallet. It’s silent, incredibly fast, and leaves a perfect factory edge.
  • For Wood/Hardboard: Use a Brad Point Bit or a Step Bit. These have a sharp "spur" in the center that prevents the bit from walking and ensures the $5\text{ mm}$ holes are clean.

4. Automating the Ovals

The SKÅDIS "secret sauce" is the oval shape ($5\text{ mm} \times 15\text{ mm}$).

  • The Cheat Code: You don't actually need ovals for many 3D-printed hooks. Most "SKÅDIS-compatible" STLs on MakerWorld only use the top or bottom of the oval.
  • The Efficiency Hack: Drill two circular holes $10\text{ mm}$ apart and use a 3D-printed "bridge" hook. Or, simply drill one $5\text{ mm}$ hole and modify your hook designs in CAD to use a circular peg. This cuts your production time by 50%.

5. Aesthetics & Customization

Since you want it "aesthetic and beautiful":

  • The "Stealth" Look: Spray the finished boards with a Matte Charcoal Gray or Navy Blue.
  • The "Maker" Look: Use your A1 to print the hooks in high-contrast colors (like Neon Orange or "Bambu Green").

Jarvis's IKEA Shopping List (The "Don't Buy the Board" Edition): If you’re skipping the $30 boards, just grab these "infrastructure" items that are hard to DIY:
